{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ebf4e46c6e97a7779f9b5a4cd6c7125da328364552992a9bae955c663b8ea030","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"New-law and checklist confusables","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: school bus exceptions, lane sharing, enrollment cards and permit holding times","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: school bus exceptions, lane sharing, enrollment cards and permit holding times
Confusable pairs from the new-laws chapter and the two test checklists; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
Drivers behind or beside a stopped school bus with flashing red lights must stop, and only drivers going the opposite way on a divided highway are excused, so an undivided road means traffic in both directions stops. [A01]
Why it matters: group school bus; confusable divided versus undivided highway.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
The trigger for stopping at a school bus is the flashing red lights, not the stop arm, so a bus whose arm stays folded still requires you to stop at least 20 feet away. [A01]
Why it matters: group school bus; confusable stop arm versus red lights; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle sharing your lane or riding between lanes is acting legally, so the driver's duty is to leave it room rather than block it. [A01]
Why it matters: group lane sharing; confusable legal lane sharing versus a violation.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A01
The work-zone reminder names three hazards to watch for together: distracted driving, zipper merges and lanes that have been shifted or altered. [A01]
Why it matters: group work zones; prereq for the zipper merge rule later in the manual.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0004]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
Interfering with a DVS employee and obstructing a DVS employee are both described as crimes under the same statute, Minnesota Statute 609.50, Subdivision 5. [A02]
Why it matters: group office conduct; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
The 30-day window governs when you start the online pre-application before an office visit, and the manual ties staying inside it to avoiding a paper application; it is not a permit holding period. [A02]
Why it matters: group pre-application; confusable window length versus permit holding times.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A04
The Blue Card shows classroom instruction is complete and behind-the-wheel training is arranged, while the Pink Card shows enrollment in a concurrent course with the first 15 classroom hours done; either one admits a teen to the written test. [A04]
Why it matters: group enrollment cards; confusable Blue versus Pink; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A04
A teen must be at least 15 years old for the written test, a different age from the road test minimum on the next checklist page. [A04]
Why it matters: group minimum ages; confusable written test age versus road test age.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A05
A teen must be at least 16 years old for the road test and brings the White Card, which certifies completed driver education, rather than the Blue or Pink enrollment card. [A05]
Why it matters: group minimum ages; confusable White Card versus enrollment cards.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A05
Permit holding time before the road test is six months for applicants under 18 and for 18-year-olds, but only three months for applicants aged 19 or older. [A05]
Why it matters: group permit holding time; confusable teen and adult minimums; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A05
For teens the six months of permit holding must also be free of convictions for moving violations and alcohol or controlled substance violations, a condition the adult checklist lines do not repeat. [A05]
Why it matters: group permit holding time; prereq for the provisional license rules in chapter one.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A05
Electronic proof of insurance from the insurer's website or on a device is accepted for the road test, alongside the original card or the policy declaration page. [A05]
Why it matters: group road test documents; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0008]
